subject: Nanotechnology
title: Strand Displacement Circuits
description: A micro-lesson that makes Strand Displacement Circuits usable.

hook.text: DNA can compute — strand displacement reactions implement logic gates, amplifiers, and cascades without any electronics.

buildup.text: Toehold-mediated strand displacement lets an input strand kick off an incumbent strand — an AND gate in molecules.

discovery.text: Cascading displacements create signal amplification — one input triggers a chain that produces thousands of outputs.

twist.text: Leak reactions — unintended displacements — create noise. Perfect digital logic is hard in the messy molecular world.

climax.text: Qian and Winfree built a four-bit neural network from 112 DNA strands — recognizing handwritten digit patterns.

punchline.text: DNA computes in a test tube — no silicon required, just base pairing.

quiz.question: What enables DNA strand displacement to function as a logic gate?
options: Magnetic properties of the DNA helix create electrical signals
Toehold regions allow input strands to displace incumbent strands, producing specific output strands
DNA strands absorb light at specific wavelengths to trigger reactions
